voyage.name: Kölner Dom
voyage.price: Admission to the cathedral is free, a 'sightseeing fee' for tourists is being introduced in July 2026 (worshippers and those attending Mass still enter for free). Admission to the South Tower costs €8 (reduced €4, family €20), and admission to the Treasury is also €8 (reduced €4, family €20). A combined ticket for the tower and the treasury is available for €12 (reduced €6, family €30). No luggage or large bags may be carried inside; lockers are available at the nearby station or the service centre
voyage.content: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this monumental cathedral took 632 years to complete, finally being consecrated in 1880. Cologne's Dom is the first thing you will notice when leaving through the main exit of the central station. If you don't see it, you've likely taken the back exit. If you are in good shape, you can climb the 509 stairs to the top of the south tower. The round trip takes about an hour and requires com

voyage.name: Basilica of St. Cunibert
voyage.content: St. Kunibert is the youngest of Cologne’s 12 Romanesque churches, famous for the Kunibertuspütz. According to local legend, Cologne’s babies are born in this crypt well rather than being delivered by the stork. The church is a treasure trove of medieval art, housing the city's oldest stained-glass windows (c. 1230) and the golden shrines of Saint Kunibert and the Ewaldi brothers.

voyage.name: Basilica of St. Severin
voyage.content: St. Severin' is the second tallest of Cologne's Romanesque churches (79 m), dedicated to the patron saint of rain who is said to protect the city from drought. Visitors can walk beneath the elevated 19th-century shrine to receive a "blessing from above." The church is a treasure trove for history buffs, housing the largest preserved medieval silk fabric in the world (4th–10th century) and a crypt built over ancient R

voyage.name: St. Maria Lyskirchen
voyage.content: St. Maria in Lyskirchen is the smallest of Cologne’s twelve Romanesque churches, famous for its remarkably well-preserved 13th-century ceiling frescoes, the only ones of their kind to survive largely intact in the city. Located near the Rhine, it has long been the traditional church of the river boatmen and houses the beautiful "Schiffermadonna" (Boatmen's Madonna), a late Gothic wooden statue from around 1420.

voyage.name: St. Andrew's Church
voyage.content: St. Andreas Church is a notable example of the transition from Romanesque to Gothic architecture and contains a 14th-century crypt where the scholar Albertus Magnus is buried. The interior is characterized by a series of contemporary stained-glass windows by Markus Lüpertz and features significant medieval furnishings, including 15th-century choir stalls and the gilded Maccabee Shrine.

voyage.name: Basilica of the Holy Apostles
voyage.content: A Romanesque basilica featuring a cloverleaf-shaped choir and a 67-meter-high west tower. Sightseeing is only possible outside of service hours. Group tours must be arranged in advance via the parish office; information on public guided tours is available on their website.

voyage.name: St. Gereon's Basilica
voyage.content: One of Germany's oldest churches, built on the foundations of a late antique oval structure. It is famous for its unique decagonal dome and elliptical floor plan. Please note that sightseeing is restricted to times outside of religious services. For details on public tours or to register group visits, please consult the official website.

voyage.name: Basilica of St. Ursula
voyage.content: One of Germany's oldest continuously used churches, with origins dating back to the Roman era. It is best known for the "Golden Chamber," a historic ossuary, and its significance as a site of pilgrimage. Access for sightseeing is limited to times outside of services; for guided tour schedules and group reservations, please visit the official website.

voyage.name: St. Pantaleon's Church
voyage.content: An early Romanesque basilica in the southern part of the Old Town, once serving as the church for a Benedictine abbey. It is dedicated to St. Pantaleon, St. Cosmas, and St. Damian. Sightseeing is restricted to times outside of religious services; information regarding public tours and group registrations can be found on the official website.

voyage.name: St. Maria im Kapitol
voyage.content: The oldest and largest of Cologne's Romanesque churches, built upon the foundations of a Roman temple. Its unique floor plan is modeled after the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem and houses treasures such as an 11th-century carved wooden door and a 14th-century crucifix. Sightseeing is limited to times outside of religious services.

voyage.name: Groß-St. Martin
voyage.content: A landmark Romanesque basilica in the Old Town, characterized by its distinctive trefoil choir and soaring crossing tower. It was founded around 960 AD as a Benedictine monastery. The current structure dates to the 12th and 13th centuries. Sightseeing is limited to times outside of religious services; information regarding public guided tours and group visits can be found on the official website.

voyage.name: St. George's Church
voyage.content: Founded in 1059, this basilica is noted for its Roman-era columns and vaulted architecture that earned it the nickname "Ravenna on the Rhine." It stands on the site of a former Roman guard post. Sightseeing is restricted to times outside of religious services; for information on public tours and group registrations, please visit the official website.

voyage.name: St. Cecilia's Church
voyage.content: A Staufen-period pillar basilica and one of Cologne's twelve great Romanesque churches. It features notable historical elements such as a 12th-century tympanum and remnants of Ottonian architecture. Since 1956, the church building has housed the Museum Schnütgen, which showcases an extensive collection of medieval religious art.

voyage.name: Die Kölner Synagoge
voyage.content: The Cologne Synagogue is architecturally striking for its dark, monumental style. Its Torah scroll has a significant history, having been rescued by a Catholic priest from another synagogue during the Nazi era. In 2005, Pope Benedict XVI visited the site, marking only the second time in history that a pope had visited a synagogue. Guided tours are available; please consult the official website for schedules and booki

voyage.name: Historisches Rathaus
voyage.content: The Cologne City Hall is Germany’s oldest functioning municipal building, with origins dating back to the 12th century. The complex is defined by the 15th-century Gothic tower, which served as a symbol of the city's guilds, and the 16th-century Renaissance "Laube," a loggia representing the civic pride of Cologne's citizens. Notable features include the "Platz-Jabbeck," a carved wooden figure on the tower that sticks

voyage.name: Praetorium
voyage.hours: It is closed due to construction work, expected to open by the end of 2028
voyage.content: The Praetorium served as the administrative headquarters of the Roman governor in Cologne, then the capital of the province of Germania Inferior. As one of the most significant Roman palaces along the Rhine, it functioned as the political and administrative center of the region for centuries. Today, visitors can explore the excavated foundations of this multi-phase structure, with the 4th-century monumental palace re

voyage.name: Gürzenich dance hall
voyage.content: The Gürzenich is a municipal concert and event hall, best known for its late Gothic façade completed in 1447. It was built as a venue for public festivities. It retains its historic architectural character while functioning as a modern facility for congresses, concerts, and social events. It serves as a representative example of 15th-century civic architecture in Cologne

voyage.name: ruins of Roman city walls and two towers
Nordtor
voyage.content: Ruins of Roman city wall gate

voyage.name: Agnesviertel
voyage.content: In the bohemian Agnesviertel, you can find independent designers, bookshops, bars, and art galleries. There are also historical monuments, such as the North City Gate or Eigelsteintorburg in the Agnesviertel, very near to Fort X, built to protect the city from French attacks, and Agneskirche, a late neo-gothic church on the boulevardesque Neusserstraße. Neusserstraße also has a yoga school, an Aikido school, a Japane

voyage.name: Martinsviertel / Altstadt
voyage.content: Old town between Rhine, Heumarkt, Alter Markt and Dom, (Cologne Cathedral).

voyage.name: Kwartier Latäng/Studentenviertel
voyage.content: This student neighbourhood takes its name from the Parisian Quartier Latin. It is centred on the Zülpicher Straße and provides ample nightlife opportunities, ranging from a night shop (Späti) with dancefloor and toilets, to grimy indie bars. Middle Eastern food is also easy to be found here, including the famous and very popular Habibi. The neighbourhood can be accessed by going to the station "Zülpicher Platz".

voyage.name: Hohenzollern Bridge
voyage.content: Also called the Locking Bridge. If you walk to the back of the Kölner Dom along a straight path, there is a bridge on the Rhine to your right that is covered in padlocks. The locks are placed there by couples to show their loyalty to each other. Couples often have their names and a significant date inscribed on the locks. There are other places around the world that have "love padlocks".

voyage.name: Rheinauhafen
voyage.content: This completely rebuilt area combines modern extravagant architecture with historical harbour buildings. The old Rheinauhafen opened in 1898 and became necessary due to increasing amount of freight traffic. The new Rheinauhafen is a mix of office buildings and apartment buildings and gastronomy. On a peninsula of the Rhine (1 km south of Heumarkt) it is an invitation for a beautiful walk along the river or for having

voyage.name: Flora and Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Cologne Botanical garden. The tropical house and the cactus houses are being rebuilt as of Oct 2024.

voyage.name: Museum Ludwig
voyage.hours: Tue–Sun 10:00-18:00, first Thu of the month 10:00-22:00
voyage.content: A museum of modern art, near the central railway station and the Cathedral hosts a worthy regular exhibition and temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Museum für Angewandte Kunst
voyage.price: Regular €4, reduced €2, permanent and special exhibitions: price varies from being free to €6
voyage.content: The Museum of Applied Art has a collection of popular design items, as well as temporary exhibitions. The historical collections have been closed for several years due to refurbishment and new exhibition concept.

voyage.name: Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud
voyage.price: Permanent collection and special exhibition: €8-12, reduced €4.50-8
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, every 1st and 3rd Thu of the month until 21:00
voyage.content: The Wallraf-Richartz Museum is an art gallery with a collection of fine art from the medieval period through to the early 20th century.

voyage.name: Römisch-Germanisches Museum
voyage.content: Römisch-Germanisches Museum explores the history of Roman history in Cologne and the surrounding area. The permanent exhibition is now located in the Belgian House (Cäcilienstraße 46, near Neumarkt). The exhibits of the Dionysos mosaic and Poblicius tomb are closed as of May 2022.

voyage.name: Rautenstrauch-Joest-Museum für Völkerkunde
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Thu 10:00-20:00, first Thu of the month 10:00-22:00
voyage.content: North Rhine-Westphalia's only ethnological museum, it has a fine collection of Amerindian and Austro-Polynesian artefacts.

voyage.name: Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst
voyage.hours: Tue–Sun 11:00-17:00, first Thu of the month 11:00-22:00
voyage.content: Art, music, books, films and culture from Asia.

voyage.name: Kolumba
voyage.content: A Christian art museum. An architectural wonder designed by Peter Zumthor and a feast for the senses; this museum, built in concordance with the ancient foundations of the shrine of Mary in the rubble contains a selection of historical and contemporary religious art. Worth visiting just to explore the spiritually inspiring spaces and the beautiful walkway through the ruins of the past.

voyage.name: Schokoladenmuseum Köln
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat Sun holidays 10:00-18:00, last admittance one hour before closing
voyage.content: Chocolate museum in Cologne. It's a short visit but very interesting exhibits. Admission €13.50, concessions €8.50, family pass €34.50 (surcharge on weekends).

voyage.name: NS-Dokumentationszentrum
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-19:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.content: "NS" is short for National Socialist. Former headquarters of the Cologne Gestapo, with prison cells. Now the largest regional memorial site in Germany for the victims of the Nazis. Library, media and exhibitions. Near subway stop "Appellhofplatz".

voyage.name: Käthe Kollwitz Museum
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-18:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.content: Dedicated to the artist Käthe Kollwitz (1867-1945), the first woman elected to the Prussian Academy of Arts.

voyage.name: Cologne City Museum
voyage.hours: Tue 10:00 to 20:00, Wed-Sun 10:00 - 17:00, every 1st Thu of each month: 10:00 - 22:00
voyage.content: Shows exhibits and works of art on the history of the city of Cologne from the Middle Ages to the present day.

voyage.name: Overstolzenhaus
voyage.content: One of the oldest houses in Cologne, built between 1220 and 1225, with an impressive Romanesque façade. Built as a residence for a local patrician, today it houses the Academy of Media Arts.

voyage.name: Kunsthaus Lempertz
voyage.content: The famous German art merchants and auctioneers, founded in 1845 (although the building is from 1952, reconstructed after the Second World War).

voyage.name: Postamt
voyage.content: The former post office built from red brick in 1906 is now used as a theatre.

voyage.name: Wasserturm
voyage.content: The former water tower built in 1868-1872 is now used as a luxury boutique hotel. The 11th floor (at 35 metres) houses a terrace and glass covered dining/meeting room, which can be rented out for private functions.

voyage.name: Wolkenburg
voyage.content: The baroque estate was built in 1734 for a Benedictine convent, but is used today by the 190-man choir Kölner Männer-Gesang-Verein Cäcilia Wolkenburg. It is also an event centre.

voyage.name: Severinsbrücke
voyage.content: Completed in 1959, the cable-stayed bridge provided a relief for the Deutzer Brücke. Although not outstanding visually as such, it provides a nice view of both banks of the Rhine if you care to walk it.

voyage.name: Kartäuserkirche
voyage.content: The church belonged to the local charterhouse (a monastery of the Carthusian order) until 1794, when the monastery was closed and the church was used variously as a warehouse or a military hospital until the 1920s, when it was restored to its religious function by a local Protestant community, whom it serves as a church until today. After reconstruction, it features an impressive pipe organ array with glockenspiel.

voyage.name: Dreikönigenpförtchen
voyage.content: One of the best-hidden gems of Cologne, the small yet ornate gothic gate once led to an "immunity" belonging to the convent based at the St. Maria im Kapitol.

voyage.name: St. Gregorius im Elend
voyage.content: Neobaroque church from the early 19th century.

voyage.name: St. Johann Baptist
voyage.content: This Catholic church is one of the oldest in Cologne, predating even the famous romanesque churches, as it was founded in 948. It has seen many additions and reconstructions throughout the centuries, and was almost totally destroyed during the Second World War. Its current form is an eclectic reconstruction finished in the early 1960s.

voyage.name: Former franciscan convent with St. Marien church
voyage.content: Nestled inconspicuously between contemporary residential buildings is this impressive complex with gothic-inspired decorations

voyage.name: St. Peter church
voyage.content: The lesser-known next-door neighbour of St. Cäcilien

voyage.name: St. Maria vom Frieden church and convent
voyage.content: Baroque convent complex from the 17th century.

voyage.name: Trinitatiskirche
voyage.content: This 19th-century evangelical church provides both regular religious services and serves as a venue for various cultural, especially musical, events.

voyage.name: Köln-Triangle
voyage.price: Admission is €3 for a single person, every additional member of the same party pays €2 only
voyage.hours: May–Sep: Mon–Fri 11:00–22:00, Sat Sun public holidays 10:00–22:00; Oct–Apr Mon–Fri 12:00–18:00, Sat Sun public holidays 10:00–18:00
voyage.content: The Köln-Triangle is a high rise building in Deutz, immediately by the waterfront. It is a part of a building complex fronted by the Rhine-facing Hyatt hotel and is hard to miss due to its prominence and quite easily accessible from both Deutz and the left bank of the Rhine (simply cross the Hochenzollern bridge from the Altstadt). On its 29th floor, it has a viewing terrace called Panorama, which is publicly accessi

voyage.name: Koelnmesse
voyage.content: Venue for trade shows and events.

voyage.name: Bahnhof Köln-Deutz
voyage.content: The historic building of the station now known as Köln Messe/Deutz is an interesting piece of architectural heritage many visitors to Cologne miss as they exit the station on the fairgrounds side.

voyage.name: ESSO Station An der Kölnarena
voyage.content: You may wonder what's so special about a gas station, but you will understand once you see its 1950s architecture with the unique structured roof and learn that it is the oldest gas station in Cologne in continuous operation.

voyage.name: Deutzer Freiheit
voyage.content: The main shopping street of Deutz, with not only retail opportunities but also many historic buildings along the way.

voyage.name: Kölner Philharmonie
voyage.content: Central concert hall, opened in 1986. Main season September to June. Special summer shows.

voyage.name: Oper Köln
voyage.content: Operas are performed in the Staatenhaus while the opera building at Offenbachplatz is being renovated. Season starts in Mid-September.

voyage.name: Stadtgarten
voyage.content: Concert centre for jazz and contemporary music, with a cafe and restaurant inside and a large beer garden outside which dates back to at least the 1950s. (Also the site of a great Christmas market.)

voyage.name: Metropolis Cinema
voyage.content: If you want to go to the movies while visiting Cologne and you don't know German, this small cinema is for you. It shows movies in their native language, but mostly English. (However, most other cinemas will also show English versions several times a week, so check the listings.)

voyage.name: Kölner Seilbahn
voyage.price: Adult one way €4.50, return €6.50; child (aged 4–12) one way €2.50, return €3.70
voyage.content: Take a ride with the Aerial tramway across Rhine river.

voyage.name: Kölner Zoo
voyage.content: Established in 1860, the zoo of Cologne is home to more than 850 animal species from all over the world. Highlights include the Great Ape Jungle House, the Rainforest Hall, the Aquarium, and the houses for elephants, hippos and crocodiles.

voyage.name: Aqualand
voyage.content: Water park with water slides, pools, saunas and a wellness area.

voyage.name: 1. FC Köln
voyage.content: Die Geißböcke ("The Billy Goats") were promoted in 2025 and now play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. The stadium has a capacity of 46,000 and in 2024 hosted matches in the UEFA Finals. The women's team play in their top tier at Franz-Kremer-Stadion, capacity 15,000.

voyage.name: KD Rhine River Cruise
voyage.content: Departure times: Daily: 10:30, 12:00, 14:00, 18:00; Köln-Düsseldorf offers cruises of the Rhine river around the Cologne area with an explanation of landmarks.

voyage.name: Stattreisen e.V.
voyage.content: This non-profit organization offers excellent tours of Cologne, led by volunteers. The prices are moderate and there is a huge list of tours, including (besides the more regular tours) Koelsch tours (for testing the breweries) or language lessons in the local dialect (again, in a brewery). Ask for English tours, some guides are willing to conduct a normally German tour in English.

voyage.name: Rickshaws: environmentally friendly city tours
voyage.content: Rickshaws are exotic and environmentally friendly tricycles, that bring their passengers slowly and safely to their destination. By Rickshaw you will discover Cologne’s points of interest in a comfortable way.

voyage.name: Claudius Therme
voyage.content: Large spa with pool and lots of different saunas (indoors and outdoors) next to the Rhine, north of Deutz.

voyage.name: Mauritius Therme
voyage.content: Decent Saunalanschaft in a hotel south of Neumarkt.

voyage.name: Mediterana
voyage.content: 11 saunas and a huge pool.

voyage.name: monte mare Bedburg
voyage.content: Large spa in the west of Cologne.

voyage.name: monte mare Reichshof-Eckenhagen
voyage.content: Spa in the east of Cologne.

voyage.name: Neptunbad
voyage.content: In the popular area of Ehrenfeld in an old renovated bath, to which an attractive "sauna landscape" in Japanese style on two levels has been added. Also a comprehensive fitness centre.

voyage.name: Saunas in public swimming pools
voyage.content: Some of the public swimming pools managed by the Cologne city council, notably Agrippabad, do have small Saunalandschaften too, all featuring a Damentag (ladies only day).

voyage.name: Ananda Tantra Massage and Coaching
voyage.content: Tantra massage, coaching and workshops, an open minded and liberal attitude essential because the massages include sexually sensitive body parts, however, no sexual services are given by the team of 30 female and male employees.

voyage.name: Sukon - Thai Art Of Massage
voyage.content: Traditional Thai massage institute, in the city centre. Thai native massage therapists practise in the 160-m² Thai-styled studio: original royal massage, aroma oil massage and foot massage. This place does not offer any erotic massages.

voyage.name: Galeria Hohe Strasse
voyage.content: Formerly the flagship store of Galeria Kaufhof, where it was headquartered . The original 19th-century Tietz department store on the Schildergasse has been expanded with a "modern" part in the 1950s, including a multi-storey parking, facing the Caecilienstraße and now fills the entire huge block. You can find everything there, from apparel to groceries.

voyage.name: Galeria Breite Strasse
voyage.content: Formerly the Cologne store of Karstadt in a more modern shopping centre north of Neumarkt, over the Zeppelinstraße.

voyage.name: Apropos
voyage.content: Features a Gucci brand store.

voyage.name: Underdog Record Store
voyage.content: Specialized in Alternative Rock, Emo, Garage and related matters.

voyage.name: Groove Attack
voyage.content: Electronic music.

voyage.name: Kompakt
voyage.content: Electronic music.

voyage.name: A-Musik
voyage.content: A widely renowned collection of experimental music and niche music

voyage.name: Thalia Mayersche Buchhandlung
voyage.content: The largest bookstore in Cologne; they stock a huge selection of books including sections in English and other languages. Also a wide selection of postcards. There are half a dozen other Thaila Mayersche bookshops around Cologne.

voyage.name: Buchhandlung König
voyage.content: Art books.

voyage.name: Taschen
voyage.content: Taschen was founded in Cologne in 1980 and is headquartered here.

voyage.name: Cafe Goldmund
voyage.content: A very cozy corner-café with all walls lined with bookshelves. You can buy every (second hand) book after you finished flipping through it while you enjoyed your drinks for a small tip. Also hosts small music and poetry events.

voyage.name: Weinhaus Vogel
voyage.content: Real Cologne restaurant. Nice service, good food and tasty beer. A very special ambience.

voyage.name: Thiebolds-Eck
voyage.content: A typical Cologne corner pub, as you would imagine: Rustic interior, worn bar and tables, plenty of decorations, you can meet local football fans here on match days, freshly tapped and ice-cold Reissdorf Kölsch, small but fine Cologne cuisine.

voyage.name: Curry B.
voyage.content: Very tasty currywurst with fries. Very pleasant place for a quick bite.

voyage.name: Maison Baguette
voyage.content: Fantastic sandwiches, very well served and with incredible bread. Very friendly service. Diverse menu. The owner is nice and you immediately feel at home.

voyage.name: Lizbät
voyage.content: Delicious crepes, a nice ambience and great service. There are all kinds of crepes: vegetarian, vegan, with meat, and sweet. The beer garden is nice and the service is good.

voyage.name: Vegan Revolution
voyage.content: Best makali halloumi sandwich around. Amazing Baba ganoush and hummus. Every item is flavourful and freshly made. It's a small place and has a good quality.

voyage.name: Reissdorf im Moselstübchen
voyage.content: Nice and cozy pub. Small menu with something for everyone. Even vegetarian bratwurst. Simple Colognian pub with good bourgeois cuisine and an always delicious tap Kölsch beer.

voyage.name: Gaumenschmaus
voyage.content: Clean, delicious home-style cuisine. Every day a different menu for lunch. Everything freshly prepared. Good Schnitzel.

voyage.name: Da Nino
voyage.content: A real insider tip for super delicious and authentic pizza. Authentic Italian dishes. Cool place, lovely staff.

voyage.name: Em Strüßje
voyage.content: Typical Cologne restaurant. Potato salad like grandma used to make. Really welcoming.

voyage.name: Falafel Habibi
voyage.content: Very authentic small Lebanese restaurant with traditional dishes. Kind staff. Delicious food. Good vibes. They have two stores, which serve the same food (though sweetmeats may vary).

voyage.name: Borsalino
voyage.content: An Italian-style restaurant on Zülpicher Straße close to Zülpicher Platz. Very affordable prices.

voyage.name: Brauhaus FRÜH am Dom
voyage.content: Traditional Colognian restaurant. Cologne flair.

voyage.name: Gaststätte Max Stark
voyage.content: Colognian and German cuisine.

voyage.name: El Inca
voyage.content: Latin American restaurant.

voyage.name: Selam
voyage.content: Ethiopian restaurant, opens Tu-F at 17:00 and on weekends at 16:00. Good selection of mild and spicy Ethiopian dishes served on the traditional plate of injera bread.

voyage.name: Zum Kornbrenner Köln
voyage.content: A nice furnished restaurant with friendly staff and delicious Colognian food. Service and ambience are right.

voyage.name: Früh am Dom
voyage.content: Früh am Dom is a great place to try the local Kölsch brew.

voyage.name: Brauhaus Gaffel
voyage.content: Beer hall right next to the cathedral, serves food too.

voyage.name: Hellers Brauhaus
voyage.content: Younger crowd.

voyage.name: Brauerei Malzmühle
voyage.content: Visited by Bill Clinton.

voyage.name: Alter Wartesaal
voyage.content: Nifty bar and disco beside the central station: various events & exclusive parties.

voyage.name: Club Bahnhof Ehrenfeld & YUCA („Your Urban Club of Arts“)
voyage.content: Club complex in Ehrenfeld. Parties and concerts. Devoted to a variety of international styles including hip-hop, jazz and Latin music.

voyage.name: Bootshaus
voyage.content: Serious clubbing. In an old harbor storage facility, but very modern inside. One of Germany's top clubs.

voyage.name: Gebäude 9
voyage.content: Concerts. International flavor. Alternative crowd. Quite popular. Inside a defunct factory site on the right bank of the river.

voyage.name: Club Subway
voyage.content: Various parties from Hip Hop, Electro to Indie music with a hip but laid back audience (Moltkestraße metro - next to Rudolfplatz).

voyage.name: Blue Shell
voyage.content: Small old dance and night club, loud and crowded. Rock concerts, music contests, poetry slams, parties, bar sounds.

voyage.name: Artheater
voyage.content: Ehrenfeld club. Not a great building but the clubbing area is fine. Club books good DJs and artists. In walking distance of Club Bahnhof Ehrenfeld.

voyage.name: Sixpack
voyage.content: In the vibrant Belgisches Viertel (Aachener Straße 33 - next to Rudolfplatz) you should be aware to wait long or even get rejected especially at a late hour. Mixed music from Electro to Indie with a huge variety of bottled beer.

voyage.name: Campingplatz der Stadt Köln
voyage.content: Rhineside camping site with a view of the Dom and city centre, the low drone of the nearby highway bridge does distract from the otherwise peaceful locality. It is right by a cycle and walking trail into the city and is an ideal family site (although there aren't many activities for children), rates are very reasonable and the owner speaks English. Getting to the site is a little difficult; take the tram/train to Rod

voyage.name: Camping Berger
voyage.content: Another Rhine-side camping site, nearer public transport. With 125 spaces, supermarket, playground and a restaurant. Rates are reasonable (€7.50 for adult per night).

voyage.name: Black Sheep Hostel
voyage.content: Creative hostel in the middle of nightlife – small breakfast included. There are female only dormitories, but no male only dormitories. It no longer has its own website but apparently reservations are still possible through booking.com.

voyage.name: Die Wohngemeinschaft
voyage.content: 16 rooms. Also has a busy, comfortable bar and a small theatre. Not far from two nightlife areas to the north (around Brüsseler Platz) and south (around Zülpicher Straße). There are female only dormitories, but no male only dormitories.

voyage.name: Jugendherberge Köln-Deutz
voyage.content: A traditional German youth hostel, mostly geared towards families and school groups.

voyage.name: Station Hostel
voyage.content: Basic rooms and facilities and the breakfast is extra, but good value nonetheless. They also have storage lockers (deposit required) if you want to keep your valuables somewhere safe.

voyage.name: Weltempfänger Hostel & Café
voyage.content: In a relaxed and bohemian neighbourhood, this hostel has got a nice bar and friendly staff.

voyage.name: The Ascot Hotel Köln
voyage.price: Single from €80, double from €100 (incl breakfast buffet)
voyage.content: This 4-star hotel in the city centre, not far away from the cathedral and a 5-minutes walk from the Friesen quarter.

voyage.name: Esplanade Hotel
voyage.price: Single from €90, double from €120 (incl breakfast buffet)
voyage.content: This privately-run, 3-star hotel is 2 km from the cathedral and a 10-minute walk from Friesenstraße.

voyage.name: Hotel Art House Königshof
voyage.content: 3-star hotel 500 m away from the railway station and 13 km from the airport.

voyage.name: Leonardo Hotel Köln Bonn Airport
voyage.alt: formerly the Holiday Inn Cologne-Bonn Airport
voyage.content: Within walking distance of the airport (unless you have a lot of luggage), but they run a shuttle. Park-and-fly packages also offered. Sometimes you can find a decently-priced room here when prices in town go through the roof. Nothing but the airport in walking distance.

voyage.name: Nuno Hotel
voyage.alt: formerly the ibis Styles Köln City Hotel
voyage.content: Formerly part of the Accor group and independently managed since 2022. Well-located with modern interior, café inside the ground floor and lounge in the basement, 24-hour reception, free WiFi (5 GHz only) and friendly staff. Breakfast buffet available for €15.90. Some furniture in the rooms can be slightly dated, however everything is spotlessly clean.

voyage.name: Cologne Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: A short walk from the railway station, the Cologne Marriott is modern and personal. Rooms are big and well appointed. There is an in-house restaurant and breakfast venue, Cast Iron Grill. The Executive lounge (6th floor) with breakfast, dinner and drinks is worth paying the extra for.

voyage.name: Hilton Cologne
voyage.content: Modern Hilton hotel in the centre, convenient for sightseeing. Prices go through the roof during trade fairs in Deutz.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency Cologne
voyage.content: 5-star hotel. 306 rooms and suites with views of the River Rhine. Host to gourmet restaurant "Graugans", 13 conference rooms and a spa.

voyage.name: Im Wasserturm
voyage.content: A luxury hotel built inside of a 130-year-old water tower. It has a designer interior and a rooftop restaurant with panoramic views. Price: €180-840 per night

voyage.name: Pullman Cologne
voyage.content: Some rooms feature Nespresso machines and a glass partition between bedroom and bathroom. The top-level bar George M offers sweeping vistas of Cologne from its 12th-floor location.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Cologne
voyage.content: Restaurant, bar, gym, spa.

voyage.name: Savoy Hotel
voyage.content: A family-run 5-star hotel with a huge spa area and a very nice rooftop bar. It's very close to the main station (exit Breslauer Platz, turn left, ~100 m) and has very good weekend offers. Known as the place of choice for many (German and international) celebrities.
